clue.text: Communities I left in twos, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means the letters of the words in twos are arranged in a strange new order once I is set aside

explanation.surface: A census note: a community where I left people living in pairs, which seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' says the I of IN TWOS is dropped from the pool; the remaining letters NTWOS are then rearranged, as 'oddly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Towns are settlements where people live together, i.e. communities.

clue.text: Rope stretched over a period — and what it will wait for, proverbially?

parts.note: a time is a period

parts.words: what it will wait for, proverbially
parts.note: the proverb says time and tide wait for no man; guy is another word for man

explanation.surface: A rope pulled taut for some while, and a riddle about what time is said to wait for.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'time and tide wait for no man' gives NO MAN, with GUY swapped in for man.
explanation.definitionFit: A timenoguy is a nautical rope stretched across a deck to stop gear fouling.

clue.text: Match results of being overpaid, oversexed and over here?

definitions.text: Match results of being overpaid, oversexed and over here?

parts.words: Match results of being overpaid, oversexed and over here?
parts.note: the quoted phrase is the wartime British gibe about American servicemen; the marriages they made with local women were the 'match results'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks sporting but means marriage; 'overpaid, oversexed and over here' was said of US GIs in wartime Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who married visiting servicemen during a conflict are the brides of that war.

clue.text: Hotel guest's requirement 1/we rectified after breakage of vase?

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in the answer
breakage of the vase means its letters are smashed and reassembled
rectified means put right, so the letters of 1/we are rearranged

parts.note: the figure 1 stands for the letter I, followed by WE

explanation.surface: A hotel guest complains about a broken vase and asks for it to be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 1 stands for the letter I; each half is rearranged separately, then joined in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A room looking out over the ocean is something a holidaymaker at a hotel asks for.

clue.text: Out of drug, criminal nicks presents — all over street row

indicators.note: all over means turned right round, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
nicks means steals, so the criminal holds the presents inside
out of means lacking, so the drug letter is removed from the criminal

parts.note: a thief is a criminal
E is short for ecstasy, a drug
presents are gifts

explanation.surface: A drug-free criminal steals gifts and a brawl spills over the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicks' looks like arrests but means steals, i.e. holds; the drug is E, ecstasy, and 'all over' reverses the whole result rather than one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fist fight is a brawl with bare hands, the kind of punch-up that breaks out in the road.

clue.text: It shows details of planes taking off and, presumably, landing!

definitions.text: It shows details of planes taking off and, presumably, landing!

parts.words: It shows details of planes taking off and, presumably, landing!
parts.note: reads as an airport departures board, but a cockpit instrument showing the aircraft's attitude also helps planes take off and land

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an airport arrivals and departures display; the 'presumably' winks at the instrument's name covering the whole journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight indicator is an aircraft instrument displaying attitude during a journey through the air.

clue.text: Those people, awfully considerate characters, collected for ages

indicators.note: collected means gathered up, so the shuffled letters close round the pronoun
awfully means badly, so the letters of considerate are thrown into disorder

parts.note: they means those people

explanation.surface: Some awfully considerate people have been gathering for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' just tells you the letters of the word are the anagram fodder; 'the year dot' is a British idiom for the very distant past.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from a very long time ago, an idiom for a lengthy stretch.

clue.text: Reported cost paid by men for women

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so a word for cost is given by sound

parts.note: a fee is a cost
males are men

explanation.surface: A rumoured charge that men pay on behalf of women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' gives FE, said like FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Females is the general term for the sex that includes ladies and girls.

clue.text: Doctor concealing revenue regularly has to hurry

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the doctor wraps the picked letters

parts.note: GP, a general practitioner, is a doctor

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of revenue is taken

explanation.surface: A doctor hiding income must hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of REVENUE, EEU.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee up is a call urging a horse to go faster, hence to hurry.

clue.text: Just a little discrimination

definitions.meaning: a small sample, as in a sip of wine
refined judgement in matters of style

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the word: a small sampling, and refined discernment about quality.

clue.text: She rotates road sign

indicators.note: rotates means turns round, so the road and sign together are read backwards

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, read as AI
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A woman turns a road sign round.
explanation.walkthrough: THE A1 is a major British trunk road; with the zodiac Ram it makes AIRAM, which 'rotates' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a woman's name, so it can stand for a female pronoun.

clue.text: Trendy book best-selling thus?

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
Numbers is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A fashionable book that sells well.
explanation.walkthrough: A bestseller sells copies in large quantities, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something selling in great quantity moves in volume, which the phrase expresses.

clue.text: Women, all poor, touring city

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the phrase for all poor surrounds the letter for women

parts.note: if all are poor there are no rich

explanation.surface: Poor women go round a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is the county town of Norfolk in eastern England.

clue.text: Feature detected in the other figure

indicators.note: detected in means found inside, so the feature sits within the other word

parts.note: else means other, as in someone else
the lip is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A feature found in another person's face.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is a geometric shape, an oval figure.

clue.text: As did the losing sides in classic battles?

definitions.text: As did the losing sides in classic battles?

parts.words: As did the losing sides in classic battles?
parts.note: the defeated armies were beaten, went under, and the phrase for being remembered for ever also contains that idea of falling

explanation.walkthrough: To be beaten is to go down; famous battles are recorded for posterity, so the losers did so in the annals.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be remembered for all time, here also meaning defeated in recorded battles.

clue.text: Deliberately support getting time off working in one

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word one

parts.note: taken as the word itself

indicators.note: working means in operation, worked into a new order, so the letters are rearranged
off means removed, so the letter for time goes from support

explanation.surface: Someone props things up on purpose, taking time off work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting ... off' drops T from SUPPORT, leaving SUPPOR; 'working' rearranges it to PURPOS, which goes 'in' ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with intent rather than by accident is acting deliberately.

clue.text: Standard credit of the Met?

parts.note: the Metropolitan Police are based at Scotland Yard, known as the Yard, so belonging to the Met is the Yard's
tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: The London police force's credit rating as a benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police, headquartered at Scotland Yard; 'on tick' is British for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measure for comparison, a benchmark or standard.

clue.text: Bearer of old news pays deserters off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of kilter, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: read as the plural of the noun pay, pays is two pays, PAY twice

explanation.surface: Someone paying off soldiers who have fled, alongside a stale newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'pays' not as a verb but as a plural noun, two lots of PAY, which with DESERTERS gives exactly enough letters for 'off' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper from the previous day carries reports that are no longer fresh.

clue.text: Is it used in labs that are modern more than old? Could be!

definitions.text: Is it used in labs that are modern more than old? Could be!

indicators.note: could be says the answer may be found sitting within the words more than old

explanation.surface: A question about whether a chemical is common in up-to-date laboratories.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is inside 'moRE THAN OLd'; the whole clue also describes it, an alcohol used as a lab solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl alcohol is a common solvent and reagent in chemistry laboratories.

clue.text: Dickens' lad meets Austen's girl for service in the afternoon

parts.note: Pip is the boy hero of Great Expectations
Emma is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel of that name

explanation.surface: Two literary characters meet for an afternoon church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip emma is old military signallers' talk for PM, so 'service' means the armed forces' word for the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: In the forces' phonetic alphabet of old, the letters PM were spoken this way, meaning afternoon.

clue.text: Fallacy: shot randomly, without policeman's backing

indicators.note: without means outside, so the policeman wraps the other letters
backing means going backwards, so the policeman word is read in reverse

parts.note: a cop is a policeman

indicators.note: randomly means the letters of shot are mixed up

explanation.surface: A random shot fired without police support is a flawed argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Post hoc reasoning wrongly assumes that what came after was caused by what came before, a logical error.

clue.text: In winter conference, Catherine Bartlett presents all these — and in these, according to reports?

definitions.text: In winter conference, Catherine Bartlett presents all these

indicators.note: according to reports means as heard, so a word is given by its sound

parts.note: the four varieties come in twos, winter conference and Catherine Bartlett, so they are in pairs

explanation.surface: A woman at a winter meeting gives a presentation, the details reported second-hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Winter Nelis, Conference, Catherine and Bartlett are fruit varieties; 'presents' links them, and they are given two by two, in PAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Conference, Catherine and Bartlett are named varieties of an orchard fruit.

clue.text: Do deal

definitions.meaning: be adequate, as in that will do
dole out, as in dish up food

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to suffice for a purpose and to hand out portions.

clue.text: Agent turned over gaining access to same disorganised utility suppliers?

indicators.note: gaining access to means getting inside, so the agent goes into the jumbled letters
disorganised means the letters of same are put out of order
turned over means flipped round, so the agent word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, a representative, is an agent

explanation.surface: An agent overturns a muddle and gets into the utility companies.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: current flows from the power companies, so amps are loosely what they supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Amps are units of electric current, which an electricity utility in a sense provides.

clue.text: Scottish footballers are untidy, so it turns out

indicators.note: turns out means the letters of are untidy are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish team proves to be a scruffy bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: AYR UNITED is a Scottish league football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr United is a professional football club in the west of Scotland.

clue.text: The time when St David's celebrated nurturing love for New Zealander

indicators.note: nurturing means holding and caring for, so the date contains the letter for love

parts.words: The time when St David's celebrated
parts.note: St David's Day, Wales's national day, is 1 March, written MAR I
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A New Zealander shows love at the Welsh national festival.
explanation.walkthrough: St David is the patron saint of Wales; his day is 1 March, MAR 1 with the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Retired West Indian cricketer bound by separate suspect

indicators.note: bound by means enclosed, so the cricketer sits inside the word for separate

parts.note: to smelt is to separate metal from ore by heating
Brian Lara is a retired Trinidad and West Indies batsman

explanation.surface: A retired West Indies batsman is tied up by a suspicious split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like a reversal signal but just describes Lara, who has stopped playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is to sense that something is wrong, i.e. to be suspicious.

clue.text: So-called smart chap caught in the process of decapitating native of Skaro

indicators.note: in means set inside, so the cricket letter goes within the beheaded alien
decapitating means cutting off the head, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: the Daleks of Doctor Who come from the planet Skaro
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A clever fellow is caught beheading an alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitating' removes D from DALEK, Doctor Who's alien enemy, to leave ALEK; 'the process of' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart aleck is a show-off know-all; the clue's 'so-called' points to that phrase.
